purpose: Teach: 六本木/しみじみ/芸人/クーラー/日焼け/コップ/数える/茶色

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、六本木、絶対、行ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When we were young, we really went to Roppongi. We really did.
lines.style: Wistful, nostalgic opening. Quiet certainty underlit with longing. Measured pace, as if watching the memory surface. Slight lift of wonder on the question, then settling back into gentle conviction.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、しみじみ、絶対、思ったわ、夫婦って、絶対、ありがたいって、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When I was young, I thought deeply about it — how grateful we are, you and me, as a couple. Do you remember, dear? I really did.
lines.style: Warmth threaded with soft wonder. Voice lands gently on each memory-piece. Unhurried, as if handling something precious. The question rises with affection, not doubt. Exhales small certainty at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、お父さん、本気で、絶対、テレビの、絶対、芸人、絶対、好きだったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your father really loved watching comedians on TV. Do you remember that, Gran? He really did.
lines.style: Wistful, almost marvelling. Opens soft on the memory. Picks up gentle emphasis on the verb — not performing, just bringing it back. Trailing question carries genuine curiosity, warm. Settles into small, solid certainty.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、クーラー、絶対、なかった頃、絶対、頑張ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your grandfather worked so hard in those days before we had air conditioning, didn't he? Do you remember, dear? He really did.
lines.style: Tender admiration underlining the words. Quiet respect in the pacing. The recognition of hardship sits without complaint — just acknowledgment. Warm question to him. Lands softly on the effort.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、海で、絶対、日焼け、絶対、心配したわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran, I remember you worried so much about you getting sunburned at the beach. Do you remember that? You really did.
lines.style: Wistful affection with a thread of gentle humor. Softly amused at the memory of her care. Opens with warmth, not accusation. Pace is easy, recounting. Question holds both tenderness and slight mischief.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、お父さんの、絶対、コップ、絶対、お買いになったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your grandfather bought your father that cup, didn't he? Do you remember, dear? He really did that.
lines.style: Tender, specific memory surfacing. Voice settles on the small kindness. Warm certainty, no fanfare. Question is gentle, almost wondering — the intimacy of a shared past. Closes with quiet affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、お客様、絶対、数える、絶対、お役目だったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, Gran, one of your jobs was counting the customers. Do you remember? You really did that.
lines.style: Wistful acknowledgment of her work, her care. Opens with gentle respect. Voice carries quiet recognition — not grand, just real. Pacing is easy, conversational. Question held with warmth. Settles into recognition.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、茶色、絶対、のスーツ、絶対、お似合いだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your grandfather looked so handsome in that brown suit, didn't he? Do you remember, dear? He really did.
lines.style: Tender admiration, almost a caress in the voice. Soft warmth on the image of him. Unhurried, savoring the memory. Question floats with affection and gentle amusement. Closes with quiet, loving certainty.
